name: Gemcitabine + Cisplatin (GC)

biomarkers.note: Cytotoxic gemcitabine/cisplatin backbone is not biomarker-restricted. Applies to urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (#57) and, as the same systemic regimen, upper-tract urothelial carcinoma of the ureter and renal pelvis (#58). Requires cisplatin eligibility (adequate renal function and performance status). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (BL-G).

lineOfTherapy: first-line for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma; also a category 1 neoadjuvant option (4 cycles) for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and an adjuvant option

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function and performance status (cisplatin-eligible)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, BL-G (Principles of Systemic Therapy): estimate GFR to assess cisplatin eligibility; split-dose cisplatin option for borderline renal function

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (3-4 cycles) for muscle-invasive bladder cancer shows a survival benefit
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, BL-G (neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy for MIBC, category 1)

drugs.name: Gemcitabine

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 17414 (Bladder cancer: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 d); line 155247 (GC in 28-day cycles, gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15); Table 44.5 (line ~155202)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 17414 (gemcitabine dosing table, bladder cancer) and line 155247 / Table 44.5: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle. NOTE: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G) prefer a 21-day GC schedule (gemcitabine days 1 and 8) for better dose adherence; that variant is recorded in evidence.divergence. The modeled doses are the DeVita 28-day schedule.

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Table 44.5 (GC: cisplatin 70 mg/m2 d2); line 155247 (cisplatin 70 mg/m2 day 2)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 44.5 and line 155247: CISplatin 70 mg/m2 IV on day 2 of the 28-day GC cycle (day 1 is an accepted alternative in 21-day schedules). ISMP tall-man (CISplatin). Requires vigorous IV hydration; monitor for nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy. For borderline renal function, Standard Guidelines (NCCN) BL-G describe a split-dose option (35 mg/m2 on days 1 and 2, or days 1 and 8, category 2B).

regimen.cycles: Neoadjuvant: 4 cycles (category 1 for MIBC). Metastatic: continued per response/tolerance.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: vigorous pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration with attention to urine output; high-emetic-risk antiemetic prophylaxis for cisplatin.

supportiveCare: Cisplatin: mandatory vigorous IV hydration (pre and post) to protect renal function; monitor magnesium/potassium and replace.
Antiemetics: cisplatin is highly emetogenic - use a high-emetic-risk prophylaxis regimen.
Monitor for cisplatin nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity (audiometry if symptomatic), and peripheral neuropathy.
CBC before each dose (gemcitabine day 15 is frequently held for cytopenias).

monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cycle - cisplatin nephrotoxicity

doseModificationRules.text: Reassess cisplatin eligibility if renal function declines; consider split-dose cisplatin (BL-G) or switch to a carboplatin-based regimen. Do not substitute carboplatin for cisplatin in the perioperative setting (BL-G).
Hold gemcitabine day 15 for significant neutropenia/thrombocytopenia per protocol; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 17414 (gemcitabine bladder dosing 1,000 mg/m2 d1,8,15 q28); Table 44.5 and line 155247 (GC: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 d1,8,15 + cisplatin 70 mg/m2 d2, 28-day cycles)

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (BL-G 2 of 8): cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (3-4 cycles) category 1 for MIBC; Cisplatin/Gemcitabine 21-day cycle preferred; split-dose cisplatin option; carboplatin must not be substituted perioperatively. First-line metastatic Cisplatin/Gemcitabine (category 1).

sources.name: DeVita 12th ed. (core)
sources.value: 28-day cycle: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 15 + cisplatin 70 mg/m2 day 2

sources.name: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer
sources.value: 21-day cycle preferred (gemcitabine days 1 and 8) for better dose adherence with fewer delays

divergence.note: Both sources describe GC as a standard first-line and neoadjuvant regimen; they differ on cycle length (DeVita 28-day with gemcitabine day 15 versus the NCCN-preferred 21-day with gemcitabine days 1 and 8). The modeled schedule uses the fully-dosed DeVita 28-day version. The 21-day gemcitabine day pattern is not printed with day numbers in the provided sources. Cycle-length/schedule selection left to clinical review.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC) in urothelial carcinoma - bladder (#57) and upper-tract (#58). Every numeric dose is sourced to DeVita 12th ed.: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV days 1, 8, 15 (line 17414 dosing table and line 155247) and CISplatin 70 mg/m2 IV day 2 (Table 44.5 and line 155247), 28-day cycle. Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G) establish setting/eligibility (category 1 neoadjuvant for MIBC, first-line metastatic, cisplatin eligibility, split-dose option) and prefer a 21-day GC schedule; that cycle-length difference is recorded in evidence.divergence rather than overwriting the grounded DeVita schedule. ISMP tall-man applied (CISplatin). Cisplatin hydration and nephro/oto/neuro-toxicity monitoring emphasized. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
